evidence_bar.merged: The PR is merged with a merge commit, the merged head is pinned, at least one required check succeeded on it and none was cancelled or skipped, and 0 review threads are unresolved.
evidence_bar.flagged: The flag's served value, read back per environment, is off in prod and on in stage and dev.
evidence_bar.verified: A build that contains the merge commit ran the fix at runtime, and the trace or job id is posted on the issue. Automated tests and CI do not count.
evidence_bar.recorded: The issue is in its done state and carries a root-cause comment.

rules.caveat: A prod flag stays off until Shawn says otherwise.
rules.why: Code behind a flag ships dark and is proved at runtime before it counts.

rules.caveat: Use this only when the change stops broken behaviour and adds nothing new.
rules.why: A fix with no new behaviour needs no flag, but it still needs runtime proof.

evidence_bar.released: The registry version and shasum equal the tested build, and an eval experiment exists or a named waiver is active.
evidence_bar.recorded: The issue is in its done state and carries a root-cause comment.

rules.caveat: A full release needs Shawn's yes. An eval waiver must be a named instruction.
rules.why: Other code consumes a shared package, so a release must match the build that was tested.

rules.why: Eval and doc changes have no runtime effect to verify.

evidence_bar.handed: The question is handed to Shawn and the notification is journaled.

rules.caveat: The PM never decides a product question.

evidence_bar.debugged: The PM debugged the blocker at runtime and recorded its trace or job id before any item counts as waiting on it.

rules.caveat: The PM never fixes another team's code. It debugs and records only.
rules.why: A blocker held by another team, or shared by two or more items, must have a recorded trace before items wait on it.
